'''Ivan Marusic''' {{post-nominals|FRS}} (born 1965) is an Australian engineer and physicist. He is known for his work on [[turbulence]] at high [[Reynolds number]], using both theoretical and experimental approaches.

Marusic was born to Croatian parents in [[Široki Brijeg]] in [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]]. He emigrated to Australia when he was three years old along with his parents and older sister. He grew up in Melbourne.<ref>{{cite web|title=Croatian Australian scientist elected a Fellow of the Royal Society|url=https://www.croatiaweek.com/croatian-australian-scientist-elected-a-fellow-of-the-royal-society|access-date=2024-07-25|website=croatiaweek|date=20 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

He received his PhD in 1992 and a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering in 1987 from the [[University of Melbourne]]. From 1998 to 2002 he was a faculty member at the [[University of Minnesota]], USA, where he was a recipient of an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF Career Award]], [[David and Lucile Packard Foundation|Packard Fellowship in Science and Engineering]] and Taylor Career Development Award. He received an [[Australian Research Council|ARC]] [[Federation Fellowship]] in 2006, [[Australian Research Council|ARC]] [[Australian Laureate Fellowship|Laureate Fellowship]] in 2012<ref name=laureate>{{cite news |url=http://themelbourneengineer.eng.unimelb.edu.au/2012/07/mse-researchers-receive-laureate-fellowships/ |title=MSE researchers receive Laureate Fellowships |work=[[University of Melbourne]] |date=30 July 2012 |access-date=3 May 2020 |last=Rahilly |first=Annie |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514212409/http://themelbourneengineer.eng.unimelb.edu.au/2012/07/mse-researchers-receive-laureate-fellowships/ |archive-date=14 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and since 2014 is an elected [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]]. In 2010 Marusic was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]. He was awarded a 2016 [[American Physical Society|APS]] [[Stanley Corrsin Award]] for fluid dynamics research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://themelbourneengineer.eng.unimelb.edu.au/2014/03/ivan-marusic-elected-a-fellow-of-the-australian-academy-of-science/|title=Ivan Marusic elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science|access-date=1 January 2018|archive-date=14 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514141120/https://themelbourneengineer.eng.unimelb.edu.au/2014/03/ivan-marusic-elected-a-fellow-of-the-australian-academy-of-science/|url-status=dead}} Retrieved 1 January 2018.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Ivan&last_nm=Marusic&year=2016|title=2016 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient}} Retrieved 1 January 2018.</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering]] in 2021<ref>{{Cite web|title=Distinguished Professor FTSE FAA|url=https://www.atse.org.au/news-and-events/article/ivan-marusic|access-date=2021-11-26|website=Australian Academy of Technology & Engineering|language=en}}</ref> and of the [[Royal Society]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Ivan Marusic FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/ivan-marusic-36779/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
